Compute modulo \(20\): since \(3^k \pmod{20}\) has period \(4\), and \(a_n\equiv 3\pmod 4\) for all \(n\), we get for \(n\ge 2\)
\[
a_n \equiv 3^{a_{n-1}}\equiv 3^3\equiv 7 \pmod{20}.
\]
Thus for \(n\ge 3\), reducing the exponent modulo \(20\),
\[
a_n=3^{a_{n-1}}\equiv 3^7\equiv 12 \pmod{25}.
\]
Also \(a_n\equiv 3\pmod 4\) for all \(n\). Solve
\[
x\equiv 3\pmod 4,\qquad x\equiv 12\pmod{25}.
\]
The solution modulo \(100\) is \(x\equiv 87\pmod{100}\). Hence \(b_n=87\) for all \(n\ge 3\), so this is the only value occurring infinitely often.

\[
\boxed{87}
\]
